 Pledged Gold Auctions Likely to Rise in Q3
 2 min read XAUUSD Shilpy Sinha Kochi: Gold loan companies expect auctions of pledged jewellery to increase in the December quarter as borrowers face difficulties in repaying loans after gold prices fell into bear territory from lifetime highs earlier this year. The fall in gold prices could particularly affect those who have borrowed at higher loan-to-value (LTV) ratios and have limited financial flexibility to meet repayment obligations. "I think Q3 will be challenging for all of us... if gold prices nearing more lows, the customer repayment will become a little bit difficult. 
 And I think growth will be muted," Mayank Sharma, business head-gold loans, IIFL Finance, said Tuesday. Lenders are preparing to prioritise collections and asset quality over loan growth amid concerns that further price declines could push more borrowers into default. Internationally, a surge in the value of the dollar and steepest US bond yields this millennium have caused a meltdown in gold prices. 
 They are in bear territory, having fallen nearly 30% from their peaks, and are trading close to their 52-week lows of $3,831 per troy ounce. Investing.com data showed prices have fallen nearly 15% in the past six months-and 13% in the past three months. He said a sustained decline in gold prices could make it difficult for marginal borrowers to repay or renew their loans. "If gold price keeps falling, then it will start building up... very sharp falls will have a problem in repayment capacities," Sharma said at the sidelines of the Federation of Gold Loan Companies Summit. 
 IIFL Finance expects the impact to become more visible in the coming months. "We'll start seeing auctions from December to the Q4," he said. Manappuram Finance chairman V P Nandakumar also flagged a direct correlation between gold prices and auctions. "Whenever there's a fall in gold price because the stage two delinquency goes up," he said. "When the gold price is going down, the auction will go up." The company expects auctions of around 120-130 crore during the quarter up from 100 crore in the previous quarter, Nandakumar said. Lenders are also adjusting their business priorities in response to the emerging stress, with collections taking precedence over aggressive disbursement growth. The focus is on engaging with borrowers and recovering overdue amounts before accounts deteriorate further and pledged jewellery has to be auctioned.
